content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read_document on candidate_specs.md and any detector/gas-environment documents that define candidate mixtures, GWP100 values, allowed operating assumptions, and any prior guidance on RPC gas gaps. Identify the three allowed candidate mixtures and eliminate any with GWP100 > 150."},{"id":"s2","description":"For each GWP-compliant candidate mixture, run simulate_time_resolution at gas gaps 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, and 3.0 mm. Record the numeric time resolutions for all simulated points, together with numeric candidate IDs and gap values if needed."},{"id":"s3","description":"For every candidate mixture that has at least one coarse-scan point with time resolution <= 1.5 ns, refine near its best coarse gap by running simulate_time_resolution at smaller gap increments within the allowed 1-3 mm range, e.g. ±0.25 mm around the best point in 0.05-0.10 mm steps."},{"id":"s4","description":"Compare all valid simulation results and select the mixture-gap combination with the lowest simulated time resolution among those satisfying both hard requirements: time resolution <= 1.5 ns and GWP100 <= 150."},{"id":"s5","description":"Run simulate_time_resolution once more for the selected mixture and gas gap as a confirmation simulation. Record the final numeric gap, GWP100, confirmed time resolution, and selected candidate ID for the reporting module to submit as the recommendation."}]}

This is well below the hard 1.5 ns requirement and better than the best refined G3 result of 1.246 ns; G2 did not meet the timing requirement in the coarse scan.
